reviewer.role: Independent checker only; did not implement the mechanism and did not edit shipping code or account files.
reviewer.independence: This review attacked the pinned revision 082981d14ae7cc1e177c9437f38da296f44b4031 with fresh Unicode and multi-dot alias inputs spanning single-line and multiline forms, root and nested ownership, and note-to-class linking.

verdict_basis: The mechanism is still incomplete at Rust revision 082981d14ae7cc1e177c9437f38da296f44b4031. A root multiline dotted alias now works, but fresh single-line dotted aliases and a nested multi-dot alias do not preserve Java's namespace ownership. The Rust SVGs contain the note entities (`Audit..._43`, `Review..._45`, `Vault.Inner..._44`) but omit the expected namespace clusters (`Audit`, `Review`, `Vault.Inner`) or collapse the note into the outer owner. Those are in-scope failures against the claimed quark ownership and single-versus-multiline parity.
commands: git grep -n "Audit\.审计_43\|Vault\.Inner\.审计_44\|Review\.审计_45\|class-floating-note-quark-alias-grammar" HEAD -- crates/rustuml-parser/src crates/rustuml-render/src crates/rustuml-layout/src crates/rustuml/src docs/parity-reviews || true

java: CommandFactoryNote uses the same CODE grammar for single-line and multiline floating notes and resolves the accepted alias through diagram.quarkInContext(false, cleanId(CODE)), so a dotted alias participates in normal namespace ownership.
Java's SVGs for the fresh inline and nested cases create the expected clusters (Audit, Review, Vault.Inner) before the note entity, showing that dotted aliases are not rendered as flat root notes.
rust: The pinned Rust revision accepts multiline and inline floating-note aliases matching [\p{L}\p{N}_.]+ and emits note entities with qualified names such as Audit..._43 and Vault.Inner..._44.

However, the printed Rust SVG for the failing inline cases contains only entity groups for Ledger43 and Audit..._43 with no Audit cluster, and the printed Rust SVG for the nested case contains Vault plus the note entity Vault.Inner..._44 but no Vault.Inner cluster.
prohibited_pattern_audit: A targeted git grep for the fresh alias strings and mechanism name found no fixture-shaped conditionals in shipping Rust files.
The observed failures are ownership and cluster-emission mismatches, not comparator slack or post-hoc SVG surgery.

perturbations.finding: The multiline root dotted alias survives with the expected Audit cluster and linked class.
Rust emits the note entity Audit..._43 but omits Java's Audit namespace cluster, collapsing the ownership structure for the single-line dotted alias.
Rust emits Vault and the note entity Vault.Inner..._44, but it omits the intermediate Vault.Inner cluster that Java creates for the nested dotted alias.

findings.interpretation: The mechanism is not yet parity-complete across single-line and multiline forms.
